[font_size=24][b]Ink Hammer user guide[/b][/font_size]
Build battle maps for tabletop games: paint the ground, draw buildings, dress them with art, light them, and export for print or any virtual tabletop.

sections.title: How Ink Hammer thinks
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]How Ink Hammer thinks[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Everything is a layer.[/b] Ground, water, walls, furniture, roofs, lights and mist each sit on a layer, and the order of layers is the order things are drawn. A lamp lights its own layer and everything under it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Buildings are made from rooms.[/b] Draw the rooms with the Build tool and the walls, floors and doors are made for you.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Heights are real.[/b] Props, walls, roofs and terrain have heights in feet, so the sun and lamps cast shadows the right length.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Nothing is lost.[/b] Every edit can be undone with [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]Z[/color][/code], and your map is autosaved every 2 minutes.[/indent]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Tip[/b]Press [code][color=#efe3c6]/[/color][/code] anywhere in this guide to search it.

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Install and first launch[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]Ink Hammer runs from its own folder. There is no installer: unzip it and start it.[/color]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Windows will warn you the first time. This is expected.[/b] Ink Hammer has no installer and changes nothing on your system: you unzip the folder and run [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer.exe[/color][/code]. Because this beta is not code-signed yet, Windows SmartScreen shows a blue box saying [b][color=#efe3c6]Windows protected your PC[/color][/b] and "unknown publisher". Click [b][color=#efe3c6]More info[/color][/b], then [b][color=#efe3c6]Run anyway[/color][/b]. You only need to do this once. Some antivirus programs may also ask about it; allow [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer.exe[/color][/code] from the folder you unzipped. Only run a copy you downloaded from the official store page (itch.io, Payhip or Steam).

[/cell][/table]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Beta software[/b] Ink Hammer is in development. Expect bugs and things that don't work yet. Updates, including 1.0, may change or break maps you make now: keep backups (each save also keeps a [code][color=#efe3c6].bak[/color][/code] of the previous one). The first time you start it you are asked to read and accept the license agreement (also in [code][color=#efe3c6]EULA.txt[/color][/code] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Help > License agreement[/color][/b]).

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Install
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Install[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]1.[/color] Download three files from the store page: the [b][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer app[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Anvil Pack Core[/color][/b] (textures, walls, paths, doors) and [b][color=#efe3c6]Anvil Pack Items[/color][/b] (props and furniture).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]2.[/color] Unzip all three to the same place you keep, for example [code][color=#efe3c6]Documents[/color][/code]. Each zip has an [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer[/color][/code] folder inside, so they end up in one [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer[/color][/code] folder (the packs go into [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer\Modules[/color][/code]). Choose Replace if Windows asks.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]3.[/color] Open the folder and double-click [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer.exe[/color][/code].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]4.[/color] If Windows shows [b][color=#efe3c6]Windows protected your PC[/color][/b], click [b][color=#efe3c6]More info[/color][/b], then [b][color=#efe3c6]Run anyway[/color][/b]. This appears because the beta is not code-signed yet.[/indent]

If a pack is missing, Ink Hammer says so when it starts, and maps show pink squares where that art goes. Another way to add a pack (or any module you buy): drop its [code][color=#efe3c6].zip[/color][/code] into [code][color=#efe3c6]Documents\Ink Hammer\Modules[/color][/code] and restart. It installs once and the zip moves to [code][color=#efe3c6]_installed[/color][/code].

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Updating[/color][/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#efe3c6]Help > Check for updates...[/color][/b] says whether a newer version is out and opens the download page. New in 0.9.24

Unzip the new app zip over your [code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer[/color][/code] folder and choose Replace. The art packs and your own imports stay as they are. Download a pack again only when the release notes say it changed.

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]What is in the folder[/color][/b][/font_size]
[table=2][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]Folder or file[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]What it holds[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]Ink Hammer.exe[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]The program.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]Modules[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]The art packs ([code][color=#efe3c6]anvilnink.pack-core[/color][/code], [code][color=#efe3c6]anvilnink.pack-items[/color][/code]) and the built-in tool plugins. Turn any of them off in [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Modules...[/color][/b][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]Anvil Pack[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Your own imports, saved prefabs and wall or path sets. Images you copy in here show up the next time you start Ink Hammer (or after [b][color=#efe3c6]Rescan[/color][/b]).[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]maps[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Where new maps are saved unless you pick another folder.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]exports[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Where exports go unless you pick another folder.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]mcp[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]The connector that lets Claude work in Ink Hammer (see [url=claude.html]Connect Claude[/url]).[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]docs[/color][/code][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]This guide. Open [code][color=#efe3c6]docs\index.html[/color][/code] any time, or use [b][color=#efe3c6]Help > User guide[/color][/b] in the app.[/cell][/table]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]What you need[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A graphics card with Vulkan support (most cards from the last ten years; DirectX 12 is used if Vulkan is missing). Water and lighting are drawn on the graphics card, so a dedicated card is smoothest. On a laptop with built-in graphics, see [url=troubleshooting.html#the-editor-feels-slow]The editor feels slow[/url].[/indent]

sections.title: The start screen
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]The start screen[/b][/font_size]
Ink Hammer opens on the start screen. Click the numbers to see what each part does.

[img]img/start.jpg[/img]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]1.[/color] [b]New map[/b]: Opens the new map form: name, folder, size in squares and grid look.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]2.[/color] [b]Open map[/b]: Opens any [code].anvilmap[/code] file on your computer.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]3.[/color] [b]Asset Manager[/b]: Browse, tag and import art before you start a map.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]4.[/color] [b]User guide[/b]: Opens this guide in your browser. It is also in [b][color=#efe3c6]Help > User guide[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]5.[/color] [b]Continue to the editor[/b]: Goes to the editor with an empty map, or the map you had open.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]6.[/color] [b]Recent maps[/b]: Your last maps with a small picture and their size. Double-click one to open it. Maps joined as floors or side maps show as one card (the main map, with how many maps and scenes it holds); open it to pick any floor, side map or scene.[/indent]

sections.title: Make a new map
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Make a new map[/b][/font_size]

[img]img/start-new.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a]The new map form on the start screen.[/color][/i]

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Name[/b] and [b]Save in[/b]: the map is saved straight away, so it has a file from the start.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Presets[/b] set common sizes. One square is 256 pixels in the map, the same scale Dungeondraft uses.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Feet per square[/b] is usually 5. It sets how long shadows are and how heights read.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Grid lines[/b] sets whether the grid shows, how strong it is and its colour. You can change all of it later in [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Settings[/color][/b].[/indent]

Click [b][color=#efe3c6]Create map[/color][/b] and the editor opens. Next: [url=first-map.html]Your first map[/url].

sections.title: Saving and lost work
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Saving and lost work[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]S[/color][/code] saves. The previous version is kept next to it as a [code].bak[/code] file.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Ink Hammer also autosaves a separate copy every 2 minutes. It never overwrites your map file.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] If Ink Hammer closes without saving (a crash or a power cut), the next start shows [b][color=#efe3c6]Recover unsaved work[/color][/b]. [b][color=#efe3c6]Recover[/color][/b] opens the autosaved copy; save it to keep it. [b][color=#efe3c6]Discard[/color][/b] throws the copy away.[/indent]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Moving a map to another computer[/b]Use [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Package map with its assets[/color][/b]. It writes one folder with the map and every piece of art it uses, so it opens complete anywhere.

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Your first map[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]A roadside tavern, from a blank map to files you can play on. Tick each step off as you go; this page remembers where you got to.[/color]

[indent][color=#e8a83e]1.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Make the map[/color][/b][/font_size]
On the start screen click [b][color=#efe3c6]New map...[/color][/b] (or [b][color=#efe3c6]File > New map[/color][/b], [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]N[/color][/code]). Name it, pick [b][color=#efe3c6]Medium 30x20[/color][/b] and click [b][color=#efe3c6]Create map[/color][/b].

A new map comes with a stack of empty layers ready to use: Floor, Paths, Floor Decals, Objects, Walls, Canopy and Above Walls.

[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]2.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Paint the ground[/color][/b][/font_size]
Pick the [b][color=#efe3c6]Paint[/color][/b] tool ([code][color=#efe3c6]B[/color][/code]) and click the first button under [b][color=#efe3c6]Add a paint layer[/color][/b] (New ground layer). Choose a grass texture for it, then drag over the map to paint.

[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Left-drag shows the texture, right-drag hides it. [code][color=#efe3c6][lb][/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6][rb][/color][/code] change the brush size.[/indent][/indent]
[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Add a second ground layer (dirt or cobbles) for a road and the yard. Each ground layer holds one texture, so you can repaint one without touching the other.[/indent][/indent]

[img]img/tool-paint.jpg[/img]

[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]3.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Build the tavern[/color][/b][/font_size]
Pick [b][color=#efe3c6]Build[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]U[/color][/code]) and drag a rectangle for the main hall. Walls, floor and ink lines appear on their own.

[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag another rectangle touching the first to add a kitchen; the shared wall becomes a thin inner wall.[/indent][/indent]
[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Draw a rectangle inside a room to split it into two.[/indent][/indent]
[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Use the doors mode in the bar over the map, pick a door, and click a wall. It cuts its own opening.[/indent][/indent]

[img]img/tool-structure.jpg[/img]

[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]4.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Furnish it[/color][/b][/font_size]
In the Assets panel at the bottom, type [code]table[/code] in [b][color=#efe3c6]Search assets[/color][/b]. Click a table, then click inside the hall. Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] to place several.

[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]R[/color][/code] turns the selection 15 degrees, [code][color=#efe3c6]F[/color][/code] mirrors it, [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+drag drags out a copy.[/indent][/indent]
[indent][indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Furniture goes on the Furniture layer and small things on Props, so you can hide or lock them separately.[/indent][/indent]
[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]5.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Add a roof[/color][/b][/font_size]
Select the building and click [b][color=#efe3c6]Add a roof[/color][/b] in Properties, or use the [b][color=#efe3c6]Roofs[/color][/b] tool to drag one out. Shape it in [b][color=#efe3c6]Edit lines[/color][/b]: drag the ridge, make an end a gable with a right-click.

For play you usually want to see inside: click the eye on the [b][color=#efe3c6]Roofs[/color][/b] layer to hide it. A hidden roof still keeps the sun out, so the inside stays shaded.

[img]img/tool-roof.jpg[/img]

[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]6.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Light it[/color][/b][/font_size]
Pick [b][color=#efe3c6]Lights[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]L[/color][/code]). Click [b][color=#efe3c6]Dusk[/color][/b] under Scene darkness, then click [b][color=#efe3c6]Fireplace[/color][/b] or [b][color=#efe3c6]Candle[/color][/b] under New light and click the map where it goes.

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Lamps follow the layer order[/b]A lamp lights its own layer and everything below it. New lamps go on a Lights layer at the top, so they light everything. Drag that layer under the roofs if the lamps should not light the roof tops. See [url=lighting.html#layer-order]Light and layer order[/url].

[/cell][/table]

[img]img/tool-light.jpg[/img]

[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]7.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Label it (optional)[/color][/b][/font_size]
Pick [b][color=#efe3c6]Labels[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]N[/color][/code]), click the map and type. Pull an arrow out of the box and point it at the trapdoor. Labels can go into your exports or stay in the editor only.

[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]8.[/color]
[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Save and export[/color][/b][/font_size]
Save with [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]S[/color][/code]. Then [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Export[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]E[/color][/code]), keep the ticked outputs and click [b][color=#efe3c6]Export[/color][/b]. You get a gridless and a gridded picture, a Roll20 picture and a Universal VTT file with the walls, doors and lights.

Details in [url=export.html]Exporting for play[/url].

[/indent]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Let Claude draft it[/b]With the Claude connection on, you can ask Claude for "a two-room roadside tavern at dusk with a stable", watch it build the map live, then refine it by hand. See [url=claude.html]Connect Claude[/url].

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]The main window[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]The map fills the window and the panels float around it. Click a number, or use the arrow keys, to step through every part.[/color]

[img]img/editor.jpg[/img]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]1.[/color] [b]Menus[/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]File[/color][/b] (new, open, save, export, package, settings), [b][color=#efe3c6]Edit[/color][/b] (undo, copy, paste, copy settings), [b][color=#efe3c6]View[/color][/b] (fit, grid, size references, fast editing), [b][color=#efe3c6]Window[/color][/b] (show or hide panels), [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools[/color][/b] (Claude connection, Asset Manager, prefab builder, specialized tools), [b][color=#efe3c6]Plugins[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Help[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]2.[/color] [b]Map name and scenes[/b]: The open map, then its scenes. Scenes are versions of the same map (day and night, before and after the battle). Click [b][color=#efe3c6]+[/color][/b] to add one.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]3.[/color] [b]Tool rail[/b]: The tools, top to bottom in the order you usually build a map: Select, Paint, Pen, Height, Place, Build, Roofs, Lights, Walls, Labels, Grid. Hover a tool for its name and shortcut. See [url=tools.html]The tools[/url].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]4.[/color] [b]Tool options[/b]: Settings for the tool you are using. The [b][color=#efe3c6]?[/color][/b] button on its title shows how-to tips for that tool.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]5.[/color] [b]The map[/b]: Drag with the middle mouse button (or hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Space[/color][/code] and drag) to pan, turn the wheel to zoom, press [code][color=#efe3c6]F1[/color][/code] to fit the whole map. The [b][color=#efe3c6]+[/color][/b] on each edge makes or opens the map next door.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]6.[/color] [b]View switches[/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Grid[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Snap[/color][/b] on or off, [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls view[/color][/b] (shows the walls, doors and windows a virtual tabletop will get), [b][color=#efe3c6]Labels[/color][/b] (show or hide all labels), and [b][color=#efe3c6]Book view[/color][/b] (the map in grayscale, as it prints in a black and white book; sliders for brightness, contrast and midtones, and [b][color=#efe3c6]Page size[/color][/b] to zoom to about print size. Export > Book saves that look).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]7.[/color] [b]Speed switches[/b]: Sun shadows, lamp shadows, contact shade (AO), animation, draft detail and the void, then the render scale. Turning these off makes the editor faster. They only change the editor: exports always have everything. See [url=lighting.html#speed-switches]Speed switches[/url].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]8.[/color] [b]Levels[/b]: Floors above and below this one (a cellar, an upper storey). The level below shows through where this one has no ground.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]9.[/color] [b]Layers[/b]: Everything on the map sits on a layer. Drag to reorder, click the eye to hide, the lock to lock. Right-click for more. See [url=layers.html]Layers[/url].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]10.[/color] [b]Properties[/b]: Settings for what is selected: an object, a layer, a light, a wall. With nothing selected it shows the current layer.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]11.[/color] [b]Assets[/b]: The art library. Pick a folder, search by name or tag, then click a picture and click the map to place it. The [b][color=#efe3c6]Prefabs[/color][/b] tab holds ready-made groups (a loaded cart, a market stall).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]12.[/color] [b]Status bar[/b]: Hints for the tool you are using on the left. On the right: speed (frames per second), counts of objects and lights, the current layer and the zoom.[/indent]

sections.title: Panels
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Panels[/b][/font_size]
Panels dock like Photoshop's: along the left, along the right and along the bottom, stacked, or floating over the map.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Move a panel:[/b] press on any empty part of its title bar and drag. Near the left or right column or the bottom, a blue box shows where it will go and the panels there make room when you let go. Let go over the map and it floats.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Resize:[/b] edges light up orange under the mouse. Drag the line between two docked panels to share the room differently, a column's edge to make it wider or narrower, the top of the bottom panels to make them taller.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]A panel's own height:[/b] drag the outer top or bottom line of a docked panel (one with no other panel against it) and it keeps that height, held at the other edge: drag the 3D view's top line down and it shrinks to the bottom of its column. Double-click that line to let it share the column again.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A panel at the bottom of the left column, below the tool buttons, fills the corner under them.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Tool buttons:[/b] drag them by the small handle at the top; drag them to the left edge to put them back.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Floating panels[/b] resize from every edge and corner. Double-click a floating panel's title to put it back in its dock.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Resizing never docks a panel; only dragging its title bar does.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The arrow on a title folds the panel up to its title bar.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] By default Properties takes most of the right column and the 3D view starts folded to its title bar: click it to open. Drag a divider or open the 3D view and it stays that way. New in 0.9.24[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Lost a panel, or a layout in a tangle? [b][color=#efe3c6]Window[/color][/b] lists every panel (tick one to bring it back), and [b][color=#efe3c6]Window > Reset layout[/color][/b] puts them all back.[/indent]

sections.title: Levels
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Levels[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]+ Level above[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]+ Level below[/color][/b] (top right of the map) make a floor above or below this one, each its own map in the same folder. The set button next to the file name ([b][color=#efe3c6]Upper floor (3 maps)[/color][/b]) opens any of them.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Wherever a level has no ground painted (or a hole in a building's floor), the level below shows through, lined up with it at 100% scale. [b][color=#efe3c6]Level look...[/color][/b] sets its blur, haze, scale and shift, or a [b][color=#efe3c6]Background image[/color][/b] of your own (a sea, clouds, a city far below) instead.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The picture of a level is taken when you save it or leave it. After changing a lower level, save it so the levels above show the change.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A violet fill where the level below should be means there is no picture of it yet (open it and save once) or its file has moved; the status bar says which.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Save As[/color][/b] on a level offers to copy the whole set into the new folder, so the links keep working.[/indent]

sections.title: Moving around the map
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Moving around the map[/b][/font_size]
[table=2][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]To do this[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]Do this[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Pan[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Middle mouse drag, or hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Space[/color][/code] and drag[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Zoom[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Mouse wheel, or the [b][color=#efe3c6]-[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]+[/color][/b] in the status bar[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]See the whole map[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]F1[/color][/code] or [b][color=#efe3c6]Fit[/color][/b] in the status bar[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Get out of anything[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][code][color=#efe3c6]Esc[/color][/code] cancels what you are doing, then goes back to the Select tool[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Selecting and changing things
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Selecting and changing things[/b][/font_size]
With the Select tool ([code][color=#efe3c6]V[/color][/code]):

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Click to select, drag to move. Drag a corner to scale, drag just outside a corner to turn.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag on an empty part of the map to draw a box round several things. [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+click adds or removes one. [code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code]+click picks the next thing in a stack.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+drag drags out a copy. [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]D[/color][/code] duplicates.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]R[/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]R[/color][/code] turn 15 degrees, [code][color=#efe3c6]F[/color][/code] mirrors, [code][color=#efe3c6][lb][/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6][rb][/color][/code] scale, arrow keys nudge.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Right-click anything for its menu: tint, flip, turn 90 degrees, bring to front, move to a layer, group into a layer, add a mask, link, make a prefab, distort, hide, lock, delete. Buildings and roofs have one too, with [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties...[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Edit walls, rooms and doors[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The number box beside a slider takes the value in the units it shows: type 3 in a door width shown in feet and press [code][color=#efe3c6]Enter[/color][/code] for a 3 ft door.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] With two or more things picked, the align bar over the map lines them up in a row or column, or spaces them evenly. It works on the points of a line you are editing and on Build-tool corners too.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Anything past the edge of the map (a prop hanging over it, a side map) sits under a grey veil, so you can see where the map ends. You can still click and edit it; exports are not affected.[/indent]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Copy a look[/b][code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]C[/color][/code] copies how one thing looks; [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]V[/color][/code] pastes that look onto others of the same kind.

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]The tools[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]The tool rail on the left, in the order you usually build a map. Pick a tool below to see its panel and what it does. Click any picture to see it full size.[/color]

sections.title: Select
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Select[/color][/b][/font_size]
Click, move, scale and turn anything on the map. This is where you end up after placing something, and [code][color=#efe3c6]Esc[/color][/code] always brings you back here.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag a corner to scale, just outside a corner to turn. Arrow keys nudge ([code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] moves further).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag on empty map to box-select: the box picks everything it touches, by its real shape (part of a road or a wall is enough). [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+drag drags out a copy.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Right-click for the object menu: tint, flip, turn 90 degrees, front or back, move to layer, link ([code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]G[/color][/code]), make a prefab, distort, hide ([code][color=#efe3c6]H[/color][/code]), lock ([code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]L[/color][/code]).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Properties (right) shows the settings of what you picked, in the same order for every kind of thing: its own settings first, then Placement (name, layer, position, turn, size), Look (opacity, tint, blend, flip), Height and Sun. Settings that do nothing for that kind of thing are hidden.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] With different kinds of things selected, Properties shows only the settings they all have. New in 0.9.24[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Look > Flip[/color][/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Left-right[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Top-bottom[/color][/b] mirror the whole selection as one piece. [code][color=#efe3c6]F[/color][/code] flips a single thing. See [url=walls.html#flip]Flip[/url]. New in 0.9.24[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pick two or more things (or two or more points of a line while editing it) and the bar over the map shows [b][color=#efe3c6]Align in a row[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Align in a column[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Space evenly across[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Space evenly down[/color][/b] (spacing needs three or more; the end ones stay put).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Distort (right-click > Distort...): drag the corners, edges or grid lines to bend the picture ([code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] keeps a move straight). To cut your own lines, turn on [b][color=#efe3c6]Slice[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]S[/color][/code]) and click or drag along an edge or line where you want the cut: a new line runs across the picture there, with points you can drag. [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] snaps the cut to eighths, [code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code]+click removes a line. [b][color=#efe3c6]+ Column[/color][/b] / [b][color=#efe3c6]+ Row[/color][/b] split the widest part in half. [code][color=#efe3c6]Enter[/color][/code] or [code][color=#efe3c6]Esc[/color][/code] when done.[/indent]

sections.title: Paint
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Paint[/color][/b][/font_size]
Paints ground textures, water, roofs and the void (the darkness around a cave) onto the current layer. Pick a ground, water or void layer in Layers first; the panel changes with the layer kind.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Brush size, strength, softness and a rough edge that follows the texture (stones and tufts show first).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+drag on the map changes the brush size and softness.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] while painting for a straight line: it runs along whichever way the stroke first moves. Let go of [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] to paint freely again.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Shape modes paint rectangles or click-the-corners shapes, handy for water and roofs.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Each ground layer has its own look: turn, scale, tint, brightness, contrast.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The row of buttons at the top of the panel adds a new paint layer at any time: ground, water, void, mist, roof or rain. The kind you are painting now is lit up.[/indent]

[img]img/panel-paint.jpg[/img]

[img]img/tool-paint.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Pen
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Pen[/color][/b][/font_size]
Draw any line, then decide what it is: a path, bridge, wall, cliff, waterfall, fire, a line of assets, a floor or stairs.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Click to add points. Double-click, [code][color=#efe3c6]Enter[/color][/code] or right-click finishes; click the first point to close the shape. Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] as you finish to draw another.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Change what a line is (path, wall, cliff...) any time in Properties.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Each point has its own width. Right-click a point or segment to split, delete, straighten, bend or close the shape.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Paths take textured style sets with end caps and corners. A bridge has its own deck height and casts a shadow into the drop.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Pen > Stairs[/color][/b] drags out freestanding stairs anywhere. Pick a look in Properties: Hewn block, Worn temple, Ruined, Rough cave, Dark wood or Weathered planks each mix their own step pieces and colour, so two flights on one map need not look the same.[/indent]

[img]img/panel-path.jpg[/img]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Curves and handles[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Click and drag while drawing to pull a point out into a curve. The yellow handle shows the curve's direction.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag the square at the end of a yellow handle to turn the curve. The other side turns with it, so the line stays smooth. Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code] to break the point and move one side on its own, for a sharp twist.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Handles snap back to a standard length (about a third of the way to the next point) when you let go. Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] as you let go to keep the length you dragged.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] On a finished line, double-click it to edit, then click a point in [b][color=#efe3c6]Move points[/color][/b] or [b][color=#efe3c6]Curve[/color][/b] mode to see its handles. A sharp point shows faded handles: drag one to make it a smooth curve point.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] This works for every Pen line: paths, walls, cliffs, waterfalls and fire.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Ropes, beams and garlands[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A line that lies on something (a rope along a dock, a beam across a gap) gets [b][color=#efe3c6]Lift (ft)[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Thickness (ft)[/color][/b] in [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Height[/color][/b], in steps down to 0.05 ft.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Set [b][color=#efe3c6]Lift[/color][/b] to the height of what it lies on, so it takes the light up there instead of that thing's shadow. A [b][color=#efe3c6]Thickness[/color][/b] above 0 makes it cast its own thin shadow (about 0.2 for a rope). Both work with 3D lighting.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Cliffs, dunes and banks[/color][/b][/font_size]
Every cliff look with a picture, and the newer Breakup, Round top and Submerge settings: [url=cliffs.html]Cliffs, dunes and hills[/url].

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Make a line a cliff in Properties. Close the shape for a plateau (or a pit with [b][color=#efe3c6]Inside is: Low ground[/color][/b]). The line is the top edge; [b][color=#efe3c6]Face depth[/color][/b] is how far the side reaches down.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Look[/color][/b] sets a whole style in one go: painted rock, grey slabs, sandstone, earth bank, mountain blocks, snowy rock, [b][color=#efe3c6]Sand dune[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Earth slope[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Sides[/color][/b]: pick a rock face texture, or the [b][color=#efe3c6]Texture[/color][/b] style for sand, earth or turf sides with no rock. [b][color=#efe3c6]Runs down the slope[/color][/b] lays the texture along the drop; [b][color=#efe3c6]Slope shade[/color][/b] darkens it toward the foot.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Top[/color][/b]: a fill texture for the high ground, and a second texture in patches over it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade top[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade foot[/color][/b] blend the side into the top and into the ground. With [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow[/color][/b] at 0 this makes a soft dune or bank instead of a hard edge.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Keep the top's soft edge smaller than the face depth, or the top texture spreads onto the ground below.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Foot line[/b]: in line edit, drag the orange foot points to set where the face meets the ground: a gentle slope, a bulging face, a foot tucked under the top. Foot points have curve handles ([code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code] breaks the pair). [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Cliff > Reset foot[/color][/b] puts it back.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Soft slopes[/b] for hills: [b][color=#efe3c6]Style > Soft slope[/color][/b] (or the [b][color=#efe3c6]Grassy hill[/color][/b] look) draws no rock face. The ground shows through and the shape only raises it, so the sun and lamps shade the slope and it casts real shadows. The width is how long the slope is; with [b][color=#efe3c6]Low ground[/color][/b] it makes a hollow. A soft slope has no sides of its own, so it takes no side texture: the slope shows your ground layers. [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade top[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade foot[/color][/b] fade the top texture out over its edge.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Dunes and banks[/b] with sand or soil all the way down: [b][color=#efe3c6]Style > Texture[/color][/b] (or the [b][color=#efe3c6]Sand dune[/color][/b] look), a sand texture in [b][color=#efe3c6]Sides[/color][/b] with [b][color=#efe3c6]Texture colours[/color][/b] on, [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow[/color][/b] at 0, and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade top[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade foot[/color][/b] to blend the side into the top and the ground. The top texture runs on under the whole top fade.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Overlapping cliff shapes meet as solids. New cliffs start with a top fill of the ground they were drawn on.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Objects on a clifftop edge stand by the 60% rule: mostly over the top, they stand on it; mostly over the drop, they stand below. In Properties an object on a slope can [b][color=#efe3c6]Stand[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Hug the slope[/color][/b] or be [b][color=#efe3c6]Set into the face[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Bridge lines and bridge pieces (planks, logs, beams) rest on the ground under each end and run straight between them. Select a point on a bridge line to give it its own height.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Tall props near a clifftop edge cast their sun shadow across the top. If a dark patch comes and goes as you move the edge, it is a prop's shadow: move the prop or lower its height.[/indent]

[img]img/tool-path.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Height
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Height[/color][/b][/font_size]
Raise and lower the ground. Hills shade themselves, cliff tops get an ink line, and low ground is hazier, like a hand-drawn map.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Modes: Raise, Lower, Flatten, Smooth, Cliff (terraces) and Level (an exact height).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Steep ground can show a cliff texture or a cliff set laid along every drop.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Show heights draws the height map over the map; the status bar shows the height under the cursor.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] For sharp drawn cliffs, use [b][color=#efe3c6]Pen[/color][/b] and make the line a cliff.[/indent]

[img]img/panel-height.jpg[/img]

[img]img/tool-height.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Place
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Place[/color][/b][/font_size]
Places the art you picked in the Assets panel at the bottom of the window.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]1.[/color] Choose a folder or type in [b][color=#efe3c6]Search assets[/color][/b] (names and tags both work).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]2.[/color] Click a picture, then click the map. You go back to Select with the object ready to move.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]3.[/color] Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] while clicking the map to place several in a row.[/indent]

The [b][color=#efe3c6]Prefabs[/color][/b] tab places ready-made groups the same way. Each asset knows its size in squares and its height in feet, so it lands at the right scale and casts the right shadow.

[img]img/editor.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a]The Assets panel runs along the bottom of the window.[/color][/i]

sections.title: Build
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Build[/color][/b][/font_size]
Draw rooms; the walls, floors, ink lines and doors are made for you. Thick walls go outside, thin ones between rooms.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Draw a rectangle or click the corners of any shape. Draw inside a room to split it, beside it to add on.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Round room[/color][/b]: drag a box for a circle or oval with smooth curved walls (a tower, a well house, a hut). Right-click a room in the Build tool > [b][color=#efe3c6]Make round[/color][/b] turns a room drawn as many short sides into a clean circle or oval. Doors and windows stay where they were.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The tool bar over the map has the modes: rooms, wall lines, doors and windows, stairs, cut away, merge rooms ([code][color=#efe3c6]M[/color][/code]).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Doors have a hinge side, swing and open angle; windows have glass; archways leave a gap.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Move, turn, flip or scale a whole building and the walls keep their thickness. Turning or sizing it turns and sizes the floor picture with it (a flip leaves the floor picture as it was).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Right-click a wall > [b][color=#efe3c6]Delete this wall segment (corner to corner)[/color][/b] opens that wall. It stays open when you drag the other walls or corners, and light and shadow pass through the whole gap. To put it back, click the gap and press [code][color=#efe3c6]Delete[/color][/code].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Add a roof[/color][/b] covers the building with a roof you can then shape in the Roofs tool.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Curve[/color][/b] mode makes Bezier walls, like the Pen: drag a wall to bow it, drag out of a corner to pull smooth handles, drag a handle to shape the curve ([code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code] moves just that side). Double-click a corner to make it sharp again, a wall to straighten it. Adding a corner on a curved wall splits the curve and keeps its shape. Doors and windows on a curved wall bend with it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+click corners to pick several: drag one to move them all, arrows nudge, [code][color=#efe3c6]Delete[/color][/code] removes them, and the align bar over the map lines them up or spaces them.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pick a room for [b][color=#efe3c6]Raised floor[/color][/b] (a quarterdeck, a stage, a dais) and [b][color=#efe3c6]Wall height[/color][/b] (a ship's rail at 3 ft, a cabin at 8 ft). Props, lamps and stairs on a raised floor stand that high and its edge casts a shadow. Delete the wall between a raised room and the one below for an open step. For a ship, untick [b][color=#efe3c6]Roofed[/color][/b] so the deck gets the sun.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Floors and walls without walls: set [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls > Height[/color][/b] to 0 (or press [b][color=#efe3c6]Floor only (no walls)[/color][/b]) for a dock, a deck or a stage: just the floor with an ink edge, no wall art, no wall shadows. A single room can do the same with its own [b][color=#efe3c6]Wall height[/color][/b] at 0; a wall it shares with a walled room keeps that room's height. [b][color=#efe3c6]Roofed[/color][/b] is a toggle: under Walls for the whole building, and on each selected room. Untick it for a deck or a courtyard so the sun reaches the floor.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Lift[/color][/b] (Properties > Height, or [b][color=#efe3c6]Floor[/color][/b] in the Build tool): raise the whole building, its 1 ft thick floor and its walls, this many ft over the highest ground under its corners, like a prop's Lift. The ground, water or chasm under it stays, so a lifted dock across a river or a chasm is a bridge with its shadow below, and props on it stand on it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pictures for the floor, the wall fill and the wall art are buttons: click one to open the picker, with a search box and [b][color=#efe3c6]Textures[/color][/b] or [b][color=#efe3c6]Everything[/color][/b] (any picture in your library, such as grass as a floor). The panel is split into [b][color=#efe3c6]Building[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Floor[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Colours: right-click a building > [b][color=#efe3c6]Tint[/color][/b] colours its floors and walls; [b][color=#efe3c6]Floor > Colour[/color][/b] colours the floor only, for the whole building or one room (select it).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Merge[/color][/b] joins the picked rooms into one room with one outline, so no line or stray corners stay where they met. Rooms merged in older builds: press [b][color=#efe3c6]Tidy > Clean up[/color][/b]. Clean up also drops deleted-wall marks that no longer sit on any wall.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Floor hole[/color][/b]: an opening in a room's floor (a hatch, a stairwell, a gap in a deck). Pick [b][color=#efe3c6]Rectangle[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Round[/color][/b] or [b][color=#efe3c6]Shape[/color][/b] (click the corners) and draw it inside a room. The walls stay and the hole gets an ink edge; on a level above, the level below shows through it. Click a hole in [b][color=#efe3c6]Select / move[/color][/b] to drag it, drag its corners to reshape it, nudge it with the arrow keys, or set its [b][color=#efe3c6]Width[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Depth[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Edge[/color][/b] (ink line, raised lip, none) in the panel. Right-click its edge to add a corner, a corner to remove it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Stairs: [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade to[/color][/b] runs the steps toward a colour along the flight, going up or down. Lower its alpha (transparency) and the steps fade out toward the far end; steps faded nearly out cast no shadow.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Distort a flight (right-click > [b][color=#efe3c6]Distort...[/color][/b]) to bend it: the steps, the well and their shadows follow the new shape.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Edit > Copy settings[/color][/b] on stairs copies their look (art, colour, fade) onto every flight you paste it on.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A ship at sea: pick the building and tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Under way[/color][/b] under [b][color=#efe3c6]Sailing[/color][/b] in Properties (shown when the map has water). The water draws a bow wave, a foam line along the hull, a V of waves behind it and churned water astern. Drag the blue arrow to turn the heading; [b][color=#efe3c6]V lines[/color][/b] sets how far the two white lines of the V run back from the bow. Speed 0 leaves it at anchor with just the foam line.[/indent]

sections.title: Roofs
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Roofs[/color][/b][/font_size]
Draw roofs and shape them: hip, gable, shed, flat, cone, dome and barrel.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Shapes[/color][/b]: drag out a rectangle, round, octagon, L, T, U or cross. Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code] to add to a roof, [code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code] to cut from it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Edit lines[/color][/b]: drag the ridge, hips and corners; double-click a line to add a point and bend it; drag two points together to join them. Right-click an end to make it a gable or a hip.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Draw line[/color][/b]: draw a line across a roof to split a slope.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Faces[/color][/b]: give any slope its own texture, size and turn. Double-click a slope in Edit lines for quick turns.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Ridge and hip caps, a gutter along the eave, and a faint shadow under both.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Eave height[/color][/b] is how high the bottom edge sits above the ground. It sets shadow length.[/indent]

[img]img/panel-roof.jpg[/img]

[img]img/tool-roof.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Lights
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Lights[/color][/b][/font_size]
Set the daylight and the sun, and place lamps.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Scene darkness[/color][/b]: Day, Dusk, Night, Cave. [b][color=#efe3c6]Daylight[/color][/b] is how bright the shadows are.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Master light[/color][/b]: the sun or moon, where it comes from, how high, how strong, and whether it casts shadows.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]New light[/color][/b]: torch, candle, campfire, brazier, magic, spotlight, floodlight, window, fireplace, moonlight. Click a preset, then click the map.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag a lamp's handles to change its reach, falloff, aim and width.[/indent]

More in [url=lighting.html]Light and shadow[/url].

[img]img/panel-light.jpg[/img]

[img]img/tool-light.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Walls
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Walls[/color][/b][/font_size]
Draw single walls (outside the Build tool), and add doors, windows and openings to any wall.

Every wall style with a picture, Lift, Flip and roof blend: [url=walls.html]Walls and buildings[/url].

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A wall can be 0 ft tall (Properties > Height): a textured line on the map. It casts no shadow, lets light through and is left out of VTT walls.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Walls edit like Pen lines: points, widths, curves.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Doors and windows snap to a wall, cut their own opening and slide along it. Open, close, flip, lock or make them one-way.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Wall kinds: normal, invisible (for the virtual tabletop only) and terrain (blocks sight, not movement).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls view[/color][/b] (top bar) shows what a virtual tabletop will get.[/indent]

[img]img/panel-wall.jpg[/img]

[img]img/tool-wall.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Labels
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Labels[/color][/b][/font_size]
Notes for the game master (a trap, a monster, stairs down) that sit over everything and are never lit.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Click to add a label, double-click to type in it. [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]B[/color][/code], [code][color=#efe3c6]I[/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6]U[/color][/code] for bold, italic and underline.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pull arrows out of the box edge and aim them. Drop a tip back on the box to remove it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Show in exports[/color][/b] decides whether a label goes into exported pictures. Export can also write a DM copy and a clean player copy.[/indent]

[img]img/panel-label.jpg[/img]

[img]img/tool-label.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Grid
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b][color=#efe3c6]Grid[/color][/b][/font_size]
Turns and resizes the snap guide, so you can line things up with a building drawn at an angle. The map's own grid never moves, so exports and virtual tabletops stay aligned.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Square, pointy hex and flat hex grids. Snap to corners, centres or edge middles.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code] while placing to ignore the snap.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Grid line colour and strength are in [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Settings[/color][/b].[/indent]

sections.title: Specialized tools
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Specialized tools[/b][/font_size]
Less common tools live in [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Specialized[/color][/b] so they do not crowd the rail:

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Waterfall[/b]: a fall between two water levels with a plunge pool, spray and mist. Click the lip where the water tips over, then where it lands (more clicks bend it); double-click, [code][color=#efe3c6]Enter[/color][/code] or right-click finishes, [code][color=#efe3c6]Esc[/color][/code] drops the line, [code][color=#efe3c6]Backspace[/color][/code] takes back a point. Foam, speed, spray and mist are set per waterfall in Properties. Waterfalls made from water over a cliff are curves: a start, middle and end point along the edge with curve handles, and an orange bottom curve you drag to where the water lands (older ones: [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Make it a curve[/color][/b]). Taller drops crash harder. A rock or other object placed in a fall sits in the water: it slides over its lower part and foams round its dry top; [b][color=#efe3c6]Out of the water[/color][/b] in its Properties sets how much stays dry.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Fire[/b] and [b]Fire builder[/b]: paint where it burns, from embers to an inferno or a burnt-out ruin, with smoke, sparks and flickering light. Drag where it burns; each stroke is one fire. [code][color=#efe3c6][lb][/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6][rb][/color][/code] change the width; pick the look for new fires in Tool options. The Paint tool has a [b][color=#efe3c6]Paint fire...[/color][/b] shortcut to it. For a fire along a line, draw the line with the Pen and pick Fire.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Rain[/b]: falling rain, wet ground and puddles. The window shows each preset as a picture; set heaviness, puddles, wind, gusts and lightning, choose the whole map or only where you paint it, and which scenes it rains in. With rain on the map already it changes that layer, or adds another (a storm in one scene only). Lightning flashes in the editor only; exports stay still. Everything else is in Properties.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Scatter brush[/b]: paint props from a brush, a set of assets with size, turn and mirror ranges, spacing, a gap between items and clumping. Drag to paint (one stroke is one undo step); [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+drag removes the brush's props under the circle. Select some props on the map and click [b][color=#efe3c6]New from selection[/color][/b] for a brush of your own; [b][color=#efe3c6]+ Asset[/color][/b] adds the asset picked in the strip. Brushes are kept for every map. Built in: Rubble, Grass tufts, Reeds (bank), Lily pads, Leaves. Claude can also fill an area with a brush or dress the edge of a pond, road or cave rim.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Fog[/b]: fog, smoke, magic mist and poison gas. Drop emitters like lights (reach and falloff), roll it in from a map edge, raise it off water, seep it from cave walls or paint where it starts. It flows with the wind, wraps round buildings and standing stones, pools in hollows and spills out of open doors. Select the Fog group to change its flow, heaviness, look and blend.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Tree Composer[/b]: make your own trees, bushes, stumps and fallen logs. Pick a shape and leaves, move the sliders, set a glow if you like, and Save: the tree goes into [code][color=#efe3c6]My Trees[/color][/code] and shows up in the asset strip, with its own 3D shape for shadows.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Ocean & coast[/b]: a sea, its beach and its seabed along one side of the map in one go, with waves that catch the sun.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Rocks & outcrops[/b]: outcrops, pits, ridges and boulder fields made as ordinary cliff shapes you can edit afterwards.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Wall and path builder[/b]: make your own wall and path styles from pieces.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Generate VTT walls from void[/b]: walls for a cave drawn with a void layer.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Waterfall, Fire, Rain, Fog, Scatter brush, Tree Composer, Ocean & coast, Rocks & outcrops and Generate VTT walls are built-in plugins, updated on their own. [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Modules[/color][/b] turns them off and on at any time, no restart needed. Off only hides the tool: your maps still show their waterfalls, fires and rain.[/indent]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Cliffs, dunes and hills[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]Raised ground, drops, sand dunes and grassy hills are all one thing in Ink Hammer: a cliff line. Draw the top edge, pick a look, then tune it.[/color]

sections.title: Drawing a cliff
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Drawing a cliff[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Draw a line with the [b][color=#efe3c6]Pen[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]P[/color][/code]), then tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Cliff[/color][/b] in Properties, or pick [b][color=#efe3c6]Pen > Cliff[/color][/b] before you draw.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The line is the [b]top edge[/b]. [b][color=#efe3c6]Face depth[/color][/b] is how far the side reaches down from it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Close the shape for a plateau. With [b][color=#efe3c6]Inside is: Low ground[/color][/b] a closed shape is a pit instead.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The sun lights a cliff by its real shape: the sunny side is bright, ledges catch the light and a shadow falls where the rock meets the ground.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Edit the line like any Pen line: drag points, pull curves, change the width of each point. In line edit the orange foot points set where the face meets the ground.[/indent]

sections.title: Looks
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Looks[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Cliff > Look[/color][/b] sets a whole style in one go. Every setting stays yours to change afterwards. Each picture is a closed outcrop on grass with the afternoon sun from the top left.

sections.title: Breakup: ground on the ledges New in 0.9.24
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Breakup: ground on the ledges New in 0.9.24[/b][/font_size]
The ground on top (grass, sand, snow) breaks onto the first ledges in patches and thins out down the face, so a cliff top blends into its rock instead of ending on a hard line. The ground at the foot can creep up the lowest ledges the same way.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Breakup: ground on the ledges[/color][/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Top ground[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Foot ground[/color][/b] (0 is off), [b][color=#efe3c6]Reach down[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Reach up[/color][/b] (how far along the face), [b][color=#efe3c6]Patch size[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] It uses the ground that is there. Pick a [b][color=#efe3c6]Top texture[/color][/b] or [b][color=#efe3c6]Foot texture[/color][/b] to use another.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The rock looks start with a little top breakup already on.[/indent]

[img]img/features/breakup-off.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a][b]Off[/b]: the rock ends on a clean line[/color][/i]

[img]img/features/breakup-on.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a][b]Top ground 1[/b]: grass on the upper ledges[/color][/i]

sections.title: Round top for dunes and banks New in 0.9.24
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Round top for dunes and banks New in 0.9.24[/b][/font_size]
For a side made of the same stuff as the top (sand, earth, turf), [b][color=#efe3c6]Round top[/color][/b] rolls the side over from the top like a dome, so a dune flows into its top with no edge. It is in the [b][color=#efe3c6]Sides: texture[/color][/b] section. 0 is a straight bank, 1 a full dome. The [b][color=#efe3c6]Sand dune[/color][/b] look starts with it on.

[img]img/features/round-top-on.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a][b]Round top 1[/b]: rolls into the top[/color][/i]

sections.title: Soft slopes, dunes and hills
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Soft slopes, dunes and hills[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Hills[/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Style > Soft slope[/color][/b] (or the [b][color=#efe3c6]Grassy hill[/color][/b] look) draws no face at all. The shape only raises the ground, so your ground layers show on the slope and the sun shades it. With [b][color=#efe3c6]Low ground[/color][/b] it makes a hollow.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Dunes and banks[/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Style > Texture[/color][/b] with a sand or soil texture in [b][color=#efe3c6]Sides[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow[/color][/b] at 0, and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade top[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade foot[/color][/b] to blend the side into the top and the ground. Add [b][color=#efe3c6]Round top[/color][/b] for a rolling dune.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Keep a hill low ([b][color=#efe3c6]Height[/color][/b] 4 to 8 ft). At the default 15 ft a hill throws a wall's shadow.[/indent]

sections.title: Opacity and tint New in 0.9.24
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Opacity and tint New in 0.9.24[/b][/font_size]
Cliffs and the spills over them take [b][color=#efe3c6]Opacity[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Tint[/color][/b] in [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Look[/color][/b], like props. Use tint to match a cliff to a palette (a cold blue for a night map, a red rock for a desert). Opacity fades the whole cliff.

sections.title: Props on cliffs and slopes
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Props on cliffs and slopes[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A prop on a clifftop edge stands on the top when most of it is over the top, and below when most of it is over the drop.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] In Properties a prop on a slope can [b][color=#efe3c6]Stand[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Hug the slope[/color][/b] or be [b][color=#efe3c6]Set into the face[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A prop lying across the foot of a cliff sits over it cleanly, with no dark band cut across it.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Submerge: sink a prop into the ground New in 0.9.24[/color][/b][/font_size]
Half-buried statues, a boulder sunk into sand, a log in mud: [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Submerge[/color][/b] fades a prop into the ground from one side, with a ragged soft edge and a touch of dirt along the line. Its shadow shrinks with it.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Side[/color][/b]: Bottom, Top, Left, Right or All round.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]How far[/color][/b]: how much of the picture is under the ground.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Soft edge[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Ragged edge[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Dirt[/color][/b] shape the line where it meets the ground.[/indent]

[img]img/features/submerge-off.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a][b]Off[/b]: lying on the sand[/color][/i]

[img]img/features/submerge-on.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a][b]Bottom, How far 0.4[/b]: sunk into it[/color][/i]

sections.title: Tips
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Tips[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Keep the top's soft edge smaller than the face depth, or the top texture spreads onto the ground below.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Overlapping cliff shapes meet as solids.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A dark patch that comes and goes on a clifftop as you edit is usually a tall prop's shadow: move the prop or lower its height.[/indent]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Walls and buildings[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]Single walls, fences and hedges come from the Walls tool or any Pen line. Whole buildings with rooms, doors and roofs come from the Build and Roofs tools. This page shows the wall styles and the newer ways to shape them.[/color]

sections.title: Drawing walls
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Drawing walls[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls[/color][/b] tool ([code][color=#efe3c6]W[/color][/code]): click to add points, double-click or [code][color=#efe3c6]Enter[/color][/code] to finish. Walls edit like Pen lines: points, widths, curves.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pick a style in the tool panel or in [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties[/color][/b]. [b][color=#efe3c6]Height (ft)[/color][/b] sets how tall it is for shadows and lighting; a 0 ft wall is a textured line that casts no shadow.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Doors and windows snap to a wall, cut their own opening and slide along it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Wall kinds: normal, invisible (for the virtual tabletop only) and terrain (blocks sight, not movement). [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls view[/color][/b] in the top bar shows what a virtual tabletop gets.[/indent]

sections.title: Lift: walls off the ground New in 0.9.24
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Lift: walls off the ground New in 0.9.24[/b][/font_size]
A railing along a walkway, a beam across a gap, a screen hanging from a ceiling: [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Height > Lift (ft)[/color][/b] hangs a wall that many feet up. [font_size=19][b]Selecting several things[/b][/font_size]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Water, the sea and waterfalls[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]Rivers, ponds, swamps and the sea are water layers you paint. Waterfalls form where water runs over a cliff. Everything here takes the sun and lamps.[/color]

sections.title: Painting water
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Painting water[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pick the [b][color=#efe3c6]Paint[/color][/b] tool ([code][color=#efe3c6]B[/color][/code]) and click the water button under [b][color=#efe3c6]Add a paint layer[/color][/b] for a new water layer, or pick an existing one in Layers.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Left-drag paints water, right-drag takes it away. [code][color=#efe3c6][lb][/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6][rb][/color][/code] change the brush size.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Select the water layer to see its settings in Properties. [b][color=#efe3c6]Pick a look...[/color][/b] at the top sets them all at once; [b][color=#efe3c6]Save look...[/color][/b] keeps your own.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Banks get a wet edge, a band of light shallows and brush-stroke ripples on their own. The middle stays deep.[/indent]
