sections.title: Rivers and flow New in 0.9.24
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Rivers and flow New in 0.9.24[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Flowing water shows which way it runs: light streaks and tone along the current, also on wide slow rivers.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Flow[/color][/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Flows toward (deg)[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Speed[/color][/b] (0 is still water) and [b][color=#efe3c6]Flow lines[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Floating things and rocks in the water get foam around them, and [b][color=#efe3c6]Wake length[/color][/b] sets how far their wake trails downstream.[/indent]

sections.title: The sea
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]The sea[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The quickest sea is [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Specialized > Ocean & coast[/color][/b]: the sea, its beach and its seabed along one side of the map in one go. Its [b][color=#efe3c6]Sea look[/color][/b] changes a sea already made.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A sea layer's own settings are in [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Ocean[/color][/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Waves toward[/color][/b] (the wind; the arrow buttons set it to a map edge), [b][color=#efe3c6]Surf[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Wave crests[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Swell[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Chop[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Whitecaps[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Tide line[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Wet sand reach[/color][/b] for the beach.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Waves keep their direction past ships, logs and rocks, and a ship's wake fades into dashes behind it. New in 0.9.24[/indent]

sections.title: Waterfalls
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Waterfalls[/b][/font_size]

[img]img/features/waterfall.jpg[/img]
[i][color=#a3a09a]The Jungle of Falls sample map: streams over two cliff lines, with spills, spray and mist.[/color][/i]

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]From water over a cliff[/b]: paint the water across a cliff's top edge onto its face, then press [b][color=#efe3c6]Generate waterfalls[/color][/b] in the water layer's Properties. A fall forms wherever the water goes over: its lip on the cliff's top line, its foot at the cliff's foot. Water that stops partway down turns to mist. Press it again after you repaint.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]On its own[/b]: [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Specialized > Waterfall[/color][/b]. Click the lip, then where it lands (more clicks bend it).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Falls take the colour of the water they pour into. Pick your own colour in Properties; [b][color=#efe3c6]Match the water[/color][/b] puts it back. New in 0.9.24[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Their sides break into falling strands, and the water rolls bright over the lip. New in 0.9.24[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A rock placed in a fall sits in the water: the water slides over its lower part and foams round its dry top.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Spills over a cliff[/color][/b][/font_size]
Where water runs over a long cliff edge it spills as a sheet. The white water where it lands has a smooth, broken edge, and rocks in the spill show through the water with white streaks. Spills take [b][color=#efe3c6]Opacity[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Tint[/color][/b] in Properties. New in 0.9.24

sections.title: Tips
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Tips[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Water is drawn on the graphics card. On a slow laptop, switch off [b][color=#efe3c6]Anim[/color][/b] among the speed switches at the top right: moving water and torch flicker stop while you work. Exports are still pictures either way. See [url=lighting.html#speed-switches]Speed switches[/url].[/indent]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Layers[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]Everything on a map sits on a layer. The order of the layers is the order things are drawn, and it also decides what each lamp lights.[/color]

sections.title: The Layers panel
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]The Layers panel[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The top of the list is drawn last, over everything else.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag a layer up or down to reorder it. Drag objects between layers too.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The eye hides a layer, the lock stops it being changed. The number after a name is how many things it holds.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Double-click a name to rename it. Right-click for copy, duplicate, move into a group, select everything on it, and new layers of each kind.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Click the arrow on a layer to list what is on it; click a row to pick that one thing.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The buttons along the bottom add a layer, a mask, and ground, water, void and mist layers. Roof and rain layers come from the row of buttons in the Paint tool ([b][color=#efe3c6]Add a paint layer[/color][/b]).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] New objects and prefabs go on the layer you have picked. Pick a group and they go on its top object layer; pick a ground, water or mist layer and they go on the nearest object layer above it. A locked or hidden layer takes nothing (the status bar says why).[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Dragging rows[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] While you drag, a blue line shows where the row will land, indented to the level it lands on. A blue box means it goes inside that group (or layer).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The top half of a row drops above it, the bottom half below. Passing over a group does not drop into it: rest on the middle of its row for a moment and the blue box appears.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Rest on a closed group (or a layer's list of objects) for about a second and a half and it opens, so you can drop the row in among what it holds.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Just under an open group's title is its first row. Below the last row of an open group, move the pointer left to drop at the group's own level instead.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Groups stay open or closed as they were after a drop.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Working with several at once[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl+click[/color][/b] adds a layer or object to the pick, or takes it out. [b][color=#efe3c6]Shift+click[/color][/b] picks every row between the last click and this one. [b][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl+A[/color][/b] picks every layer in the list, [b][color=#efe3c6]Esc[/color][/b] lets go.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag any picked row and they all move together, in the same order. Drop on the middle of a group to put them inside it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The eye, the lock, Copy, Duplicate, Delete and the moves all work on every picked layer.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Keys while the panel is in use: [b][color=#efe3c6]Alt+Up / Alt+Down[/color][/b] move, [b][color=#efe3c6]Alt+Right[/color][/b] into the group above, [b][color=#efe3c6]Alt+Left[/color][/b] out of its group, [b][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl+G[/color][/b] group the picked layers, [b][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl+Shift+G[/color][/b] ungroup, [b][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl+D[/color][/b] duplicate, [b][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V[/color][/b] copy and paste, [b][color=#efe3c6]F2[/color][/b] rename, [b][color=#efe3c6]Delete[/color][/b] delete.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Right-click picked objects on the map, then [b][color=#efe3c6]Move to layer > New layer...[/color][/b] to give them a layer of their own.[/indent]

[img]img/layers-panel.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Kinds of layer
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Kinds of layer[/b][/font_size]
[table=2][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]Kind[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]What it is for[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Layer[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Objects: furniture, props, trees, decals, walls, lights and labels.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Group[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]A folder of layers (the new map's Objects group holds Props and Furniture). Hide, lock or fade the whole group at once.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Ground[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]One painted texture (grass, dirt, flagstones). Stack several and paint where each shows.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Water[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Painted water with depth, flow around rocks, foam and ripples.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Roof[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Painted roof cover that keeps the sun and rain off, even while hidden. (For drawn roofs with slopes, use the Roofs tool.)[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Void[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]The darkness around a cave. What it covers fades into nothing, and the open area is cave floor: no sun, lamps still work.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Rain[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Falling rain, wet ground and puddles over everything below it. It covers the whole map until you paint it: pick the layer, use the Paint tool (B), [b][color=#efe3c6]Clear all[/color][/b], then paint where it rains (right-drag dries an area). It stays off water (drops make rings there), fire and waterfalls, runs down cliff faces, and wets roofs that show without puddles on them. Rooms of buildings and hidden roofs stay dry.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Mist / cloud[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Drifting clouds that fill a painted shape. At the top it rolls over the scene; at the bottom it is a cloud sea under the map.[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Order matters
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Order matters[/b][/font_size]
Layers draw from the bottom of the list up. Three things follow from that:

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]What covers what.[/b] Canopy over Walls hides the wall tops under the trees.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]What a lamp lights.[/b] A lamp lights its own layer and every layer under it, never the layers above it. Details in [url=lighting.html#layer-order]Light and layer order[/url].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Where mist and rain sit.[/b] Mist at the top of the list drifts over everything; low in the list it shows only where the ground is cleared.[/indent]

sections.title: Opacity and blend modes
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Opacity and blend modes[/b][/font_size]
Object, group, ground, roof and mist layers, and most objects, have an opacity and a blend mode (Multiply, Screen, Overlay and nine more) in Properties. Water, void and rain layers have no blend; cliffs, waterfalls, spills, fire and buildings have none either, and drawn roofs offer Normal, Multiply, Add and Subtract (see [url=walls.html#roof-blend]Roof blend[/url]). Every layer panel ends with the same Layer block: name, opacity, blend, tint, lit by the sun, scenes and mask. A half-transparent group fades as one picture, so the things inside it do not show through each other.

Ground layers take a blend mode too, on the layer itself or from a group around it. Blended ground mixes with what is under it and is not lit again, like blended objects: Multiply reads right at night, Screen and Add stay bright in the dark.

Mist and fog take blend modes too: Screen for a glowing haze, Add for magic light, Multiply with a dark or coloured fog for smoke or poison gas (white fog on Multiply or Overlay barely shows). For fog, set the blend on the Fog group, not on the Fog emitters layer: that layer only holds the markers, and its Properties has [b][color=#efe3c6]Go to the fog[/color][/b].

sections.title: Layer masks
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Layer masks[/b][/font_size]
A mask hides part of an object layer or a group without deleting anything, like a layer mask in Photoshop: half a statue buried in sand, a prop tucked under a cave wall, a rug cut off at a doorway, trees fading out at the map edge. White on the mask shows, black hides, grey is see-through.

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Adding a mask[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pick the layer or group and click [b]Mask[/b] at the bottom of the Layers panel (next to New group). The mask starts showing everything and the Paint tool opens on it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Or right-click the layer > [b][color=#efe3c6]Add mask[/color][/b], or [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Mask > Add mask[/color][/b] (starts with everything showing). To start with everything hidden, use the layer's right-click menu.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Masks go on object layers and groups. Ground, water and void layers are already painted, so to mask them, put them in a group and mask the group.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Masking single objects or a few together[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Right-click an object, a wall piece or a building > [b][color=#efe3c6]Add mask to this object[/color][/b] (or select it and click [b]Mask[/b]). It moves onto its own masked layer just above its old one, with the same settings and a linked mask that follows it. The mask starts as a copy of the old layer's mask, so nothing changes until you paint. Good for blending one wall into the wall behind it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Several selected: [b][color=#efe3c6]Add mask to these[/color][/b] gives them one shared mask. [b][color=#efe3c6]Group into a layer[/color][/b] puts them on one new layer without a mask; then click [b]Mask[/b] (with nothing selected on the map) to mask the whole group.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The moved pieces draw over the rest of their old layer.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]The thumbnails[/color][/b][/font_size]
A masked layer shows two thumbnails on its row with a chain between them, as in Photoshop:

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Layer thumbnail[/b]: click it to work on the layer's objects (move, place, select).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Chain[/b]: gold means Linked. Click it to link or unlink.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Mask thumbnail[/b]: a small black and white picture of the mask. Click it to paint the mask. A gold frame shows which one you are working on.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [code][color=#efe3c6]Alt[/color][/code]+click the mask thumbnail to see the mask in black and white over the map. [code][color=#efe3c6]Shift[/color][/code]+click turns the mask off and on (an off mask shows a red cross).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag the mask thumbnail onto another layer or group to move the mask there. Hold [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code] as you drop to copy it instead.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Painting the mask[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] While you paint a mask, the map shows red wherever the mask hides, so you can see exactly what is cut.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Left-drag shows, right-drag hides. Soft brushes give soft edges; a hard brush gives a clean cut.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The Paint panel adds [b]Show all[/b], [b]Hide all[/b], [b]Invert[/b], [b]Black and white[/b] (or back to the red overlay) and [b]Back to the layer[/b].[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]How masks behave[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Linked[/b] (on by default): move, turn or scale everything on the layer together and the mask goes with it. Moving only some things leaves the mask where it is. On a group, select the group to move all of it with its mask. Unlink to move things under a mask that stays put.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Masks stack: a mask on a group and masks on layers inside it all apply.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Hidden parts cast no sun shadow, block no lamp light (props, walls and buildings) and make no shore in water, so a half-buried rock casts half a shadow and a buried stretch of wall lets lamp light through.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Masks work on layers with a blend mode (Multiply, Screen and the rest) too.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Invert, copy, paste and delete are on the layer's right-click menu. With the mask thumbnail picked (gold frame), [code][color=#efe3c6]Delete[/color][/code], the bin button or dragging the thumbnail onto the bin deletes only the mask, never the layer.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Two things a mask does not change: a water layer cut by a group mask has no foam along the cut (erase the water itself where a shore should show), and the VTT export writes the full line of a masked wall.[/indent]

sections.title: Per-layer switches
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Per-layer switches[/b][/font_size]
Pick a layer and Properties shows its switches:

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Lit by the sun[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Casts sun shadows[/color][/b]. Layers named Paths, Floor, Decals, Rug, Water, Ground or Light start with Casts sun shadows off (the box says so): what is on them lies flat. Tick it to make them cast. An object there with a Height or Lift is still shaded at that height.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Affects water[/color][/b]: off for trees over a stream, so their trunks make no ripples. A single object can differ from its layer: pick it, then set [b][color=#efe3c6]Affects water[/color][/b] under Sun in Properties (Same as layer, Yes or No). It only shows when the map has water.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Sailing[/color][/b]: for a ship at sea. Pick the ship (a building or a picture) and tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Under way[/color][/b] in Properties. The water draws a bow wave, a foam line along the hull, a V of waves behind it and churned water astern, and the hull stops getting a beach round it. Drag the blue arrow to turn its heading; V lines sets how far the white lines of the V run before they fade; Speed 0 leaves it at anchor with just the foam line. Leave sea behind the stern for the wake to show.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Roof (keeps the rain off)[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Ground layers stacked above objects (a layer of sand drifted over a dock, stairs or a wall) take the light of what they lie on: a wall top is bright, stair steps keep their shading, the sand sits in the shadows the ground is in. Next to building floors they skip the floor's contact shade so its edge does not show. [b][color=#efe3c6]Contact shade from things under it[/color][/b] brings that shade back; [b][color=#efe3c6]Flat light (ignore what is under it)[/color][/b] drops all shading from what is under the layer (it then also skips the shadows the ground around it is in, so a patch can look brighter than its surroundings). To hide an object's shape under sand cleanly, mask the object instead.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A building hides what is drawn under it on its own layer from the sun, lamps and contact shade, like things on lower layers (a tower over a cliff casts no shadows of the cliff's plants onto its floor).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Shown in[/color][/b] (maps with more than one scene): tick the scenes a layer shows in. Rain and fog usually belong to one scene, such as a storm at night, while the ground shows in all of them. New rain and mist layers start in the scene you are in; a new scene made as a copy keeps the layers of the scene it was copied from. Deleting a scene deletes the layers that were only in it (Ctrl+Z brings them back).[/indent]

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Light and shadow[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]Daylight sets how bright the shadows are, the sun or moon throws shadows from everything with a height, and lamps light what is under them in the layer stack.[/color]

sections.title: Scene darkness
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Scene darkness[/b][/font_size]
In the Lights tool ([code][color=#efe3c6]L[/color][/code]), [b][color=#efe3c6]Day[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Dusk[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Night[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Cave[/color][/b] set the whole scene at once.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Daylight[/color][/b] is the light that reaches everywhere, shadows included. 100% means shadows are only as dark as the sun's extra light makes them.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Ambient tint[/color][/b] colours that light: blue for night, warm for a sunset.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Daylight can go down to 0%: everything outside your lamps is black and the lamps keep their full colour (3D lighting).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Overall brightness[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Overall contrast[/color][/b], [b][color=#efe3c6]Overall saturation[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Colour tone[/color][/b] (cool to warm) grade the whole finished map; labels stay as drawn. [b][color=#efe3c6]Lamp exposure[/color][/b] brightens or dims every lamp at once.[/indent]

sections.title: The sun or moon
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]The sun or moon[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]From[/color][/b] is the direction it shines from, [b][color=#efe3c6]Elevation[/color][/b] how high it is. A low sun throws long shadows: at 14 degrees a shadow is about four times as long as the thing is tall.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Intensity[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Color[/color][/b] set its strength and colour.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow colour[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow depth[/color][/b] set how dark and what colour every shadow is.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Cast shadows[/color][/b] turns sun shadows on for this map.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow fade[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Fade over[/color][/b]: long shadows are darkest at the foot of what casts them and lighten toward the tip, as in life. 0 gives even shadows.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Soft edges[/color][/b]: shadow edges blur the further they reach from the caster. 0 keeps them crisp.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Lamp shadow fade[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Lamp fade over[/color][/b]: the same fade for lamp shadows (of things shorter than the lamp). It works with the sun off.[/indent]

Heights come from the things themselves: walls use their height, props their [b][color=#efe3c6]Height (ft)[/color][/b] (how tall they are) and [b][color=#efe3c6]Lift (ft)[/color][/b] (how high they hang: a sail on its yard, a chandelier; the shadow then lands apart from it and lamps shine under it), roofs their eave and ridge, terrain its painted height.

[img]img/panel-light.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Lamps
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Lamps[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Pick a preset under [b][color=#efe3c6]New light[/color][/b] (torch, candle, campfire, brazier, magic, spotlight, floodlight, window, fireplace, moonlight) and click the map. Each preset has a sensible height: a candle 3 ft, a torch 7 ft.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drag a lamp to move it; drag its handles for reach, falloff, aim and width.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Lamps cast shadows from walls and from every prop's outline. A lamp above a crate is not blocked by it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A lamp with [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadows[/color][/b] off is a clean area light: only walls and buildings stop it. Tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Through walls[/color][/b] as well and nothing stops it, for an overall fill light.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Stays on its level[/color][/b]: the light reaches only the ground it stands on and anything higher, so a cliff fully blocks it from everything below (3D lighting).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Object lamps (a lantern, a brazier): untick [b][color=#efe3c6]Light this object[/color][/b] so a sconce lights the room without glaring on itself.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] One building floor can take about 14 lamps. Past that, some lamps stop lighting that floor (their walls still light). Spread the lamps out or split a big hall into more than one building.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Trees cast their crown's shadow plus a thin trunk shadow joining it to the tree.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Hide a layer to switch its lamps off.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Glowing art (lanterns, crystals, runes) can glow and cast real light of its own colour; see the object's Properties.[/indent]

sections.title: 3D lighting
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]3D lighting[/b][/font_size]
Lamps and the sun are lit and shadowed by a hidden 3D copy of the map: walls are solid with real door and window holes, props stand at their real height and lift, cliffs and terrain have their real slopes. Shadows soften as they widen, buildings with roofs only let the sun in through their doors and windows, and exports carry the same look.

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Render quality[/color][/b] (top bar, and [b][color=#efe3c6]Settings > Speed[/color][/b]), 10% to 100%: low settings give chunkier, softer shadows and much faster lighting while you work. Exports always render at full quality.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]3D lighting[/color][/b] in the Lights tool, under [b][color=#efe3c6]Master light (sun or moon)[/color][/b], turns it off for the classic 2D lighting. The choice is kept on your computer, not in the map. Computers without Vulkan or Direct3D 12 use classic lighting.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]View > Show shadow shapes (3D)[/color][/b] shows each object's 3D shape over the map, and the 3D view panel shows the whole copy. Shape any asset in the Asset Manager with [b][color=#efe3c6]Design 3D shape[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Only things that exist on the map cast: a mast drawn into a ship's deck picture casts nothing. Add an object for it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Layer order does not matter to 3D lighting, only heights do. A prop partly over a step or a low ledge is lit just above the highest ground under it, and props lean only with gentle slopes, so stair edges do not show through them.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A rope or beam lying on a dock: give the line a [b][color=#efe3c6]Lift[/color][/b] (and a [b][color=#efe3c6]Thickness[/color][/b] for its own shadow) in [b][color=#efe3c6]Properties > Height[/color][/b]. Walls have [b][color=#efe3c6]Lift[/color][/b] too: a railing or beam that hangs off the ground.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The 3D view shows props with a [b][color=#efe3c6]Design 3D shape[/color][/b] in that shape. If a shadow looks wrong there, check the shape's slices reach the top of the picture.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Sun [b][color=#efe3c6]Soft edges[/color][/b] can blur a step's light onto a prop sitting partly over it (a lighter patch). Lower it on that map if it shows.[/indent]

sections.title: Light and layer order
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Light and layer order[/b][/font_size]
With 3D lighting, height decides what a lamp lights inside a room: a lamp on a table lights the floor, a chandelier lights the table. Layer order still keeps lamps under [b]roofs and high mist[/b]: those stay unlit by lamps under them. With classic 2D lighting a lamp lights [b]its own layer and every layer under it[/b], never the layers above it.

In this stack the lamps sit under the roofs, so the roof tops stay dark while the floor and furniture are lit. Drag the Lights layer above Roofs and the lamps light the roofs too.

Bounce light (light spilling off lit surfaces) follows the top lamp: layers above every lamp get none.

[indent][color=#a3a09a]•[/color] Mist [i]not lit[/i][/indent]
[indent][color=#a3a09a]•[/color] Roofs [i]not lit[/i][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Lights [i]the lamps[/i][/indent]
[indent][color=#a3a09a]•[/color] Furniture [i]lit[/i][/indent]
[indent][color=#a3a09a]•[/color] Walls [i]lit[/i][/indent]
[indent][color=#a3a09a]•[/color] Floor [i]lit[/i][/indent]

sections.title: Contact shade and bounce light
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Contact shade and bounce light[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Ambient occlusion[/color][/b] (contact shade) darkens where things meet the ground and in tight corners. [b][color=#efe3c6]Strength[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Reach[/color][/b] in the Lights panel.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Bounce light[/color][/b] lifts shadows next to a lamp's pool or a sunlit wall and tints them with its colour.[/indent]

sections.title: Speed switches
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Speed switches[/b][/font_size]

[img]img/speed-switches.jpg[/img]

The row of switches at the top right of the window turns heavy effects off while you work: [b]sun shadows[/b], [b]lamp shadows[/b], [b]contact shade[/b], [b]animation[/b], [b]draft detail[/b] and the [b]void[/b], then the [b]render scale[/b]. A lit switch is on.

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]No sun shadows?[/b]Check the first switch (the sun). When it is off, no sun shadows show in the editor, even with Cast shadows ticked. The Lights panel says so and has a [b][color=#efe3c6]Show sun shadows[/color][/b] button. Exports always have every effect.

[/cell][/table]

[b][color=#efe3c6]View > Fast editing[/color][/b] turns all of them off and drops the render scale to 50%. [b][color=#efe3c6]View > Full quality[/color][/b] turns them back on. The switches are saved on your computer, not in the map.

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Exporting for play[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a][b][color=#efe3c6]File > Export[/color][/b] ([code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]E[/color][/code]) writes everything a table needs in one run: pictures for print or screen, and a file a virtual tabletop can read with the walls, doors and lights.[/color]

sections.title: The outputs
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]The outputs[/b][/font_size]
[table=2][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]Output[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3][color=#a3a09a]Use it for[/color][/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Gridless[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Virtual tabletops that draw their own grid.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Gridded[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Printing, or tabletops without a grid.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Roll20[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]A JPG at Roll20's 70 px per square, no grid.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Master PNG[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]A lossless copy to keep or edit elsewhere.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Universal VTT[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]A [code].dd2vtt[/code] file: the picture plus walls, doors, windows and lights.[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]Book (grayscale PNG)[/cell][cell padding=0,3,18,3]A black and white picture for a printed book, with the look set in Book view (top bar): brightness, contrast and midtones. 74 px per square by default.[/cell][/table]

Each output has its own size in pixels per square. Higher is sharper and bigger on disk.

[img]img/export-window.jpg[/img]

sections.title: Before you export: Check map
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Before you export: Check map[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Check map[/color][/b] lists mistakes that are easy to miss: missing art, props off the map edge or hidden under a building's floor, two copies of a prop on top of each other, props drawn far bigger or smaller than usual, glows that blow out to white, lamps right beside a tall prop (they throw a hard wedge of shadow), lamps off the map and empty layers. Its lighting pass flags lamps with shadows off, lamps above a roof or inside a prop, and furniture that casts no shadow; it also lists art with no size in its pack. Click a line to select the thing and go there. It changes nothing; fix what matters and click [b][color=#efe3c6]Check again[/color][/b].

sections.title: Into a virtual tabletop
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Into a virtual tabletop[/b][/font_size]
The [code].dd2vtt[/code] file is the Universal VTT format. It loads in:

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Foundry VTT[/b] with the Universal Battlemap Importer module.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Owlbear Rodeo[/b], [b]Arkenforge[/b], [b]Fantasy Grounds[/b] and most tools that take Dungeondraft exports.[/indent]

Before exporting, turn on [b][color=#efe3c6]Walls view[/color][/b] (top bar) to check what the tabletop will get: walls, doors, windows and openings in colour. The export also writes a short report of problems it found (gaps in walls, doors off a wall).

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Windows in the VTT file[/color][/b]: as closed doors (block sight until opened) or as gaps.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Image inside the VTT file[/color][/b]: PNG works everywhere; WebP is much smaller if your tabletop takes it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Invisible walls (Walls tool) block sight and movement in the tabletop but never show in the picture. Cave edges: [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Specialized > Generate VTT walls from void[/color][/b].[/indent]

sections.title: Other settings
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Other settings[/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Maps to export[/color][/b]: only this map, or this map with its levels above and below and the maps beside it. [b][color=#efe3c6]Overview of how they join[/color][/b] adds one picture of them all laid out together.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Scenes[/color][/b]: every scene (one set each) or only the current one.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow and water detail[/color][/b]: High and Max render sharper shadows and water for the export.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Labels[/color][/b]: a DM copy with labels, a clean player copy, or both in their own folders.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Grid[/color][/b]: line colour, opacity and width for the gridded copy.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]Watermarked copy[/color][/b]: a smaller copy with your logo or text for posting online.[/indent]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]Exports always render everything[/b]The speed switches only change the editor. Sun shadows, lamp shadows and animation all go into the export, at the detail you pick.

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: Package a map
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Package a map[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#efe3c6]File > Package map with its assets[/color][/b] writes a folder with the map and every piece of art it uses. Open the [code].anvilmap[/code] inside it on any computer and its art joins the library on its own.

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]Connect Claude[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]With the connection on, Claude (in the Claude desktop app) can build, check and export maps in Ink Hammer while you watch. Every change shows up live, and [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]Z[/color][/code] undoes it like your own edits.[/color]

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][b]What you need[/b]The Claude desktop app for Windows and a Claude plan that can use connectors. Setup takes about ten minutes, once.

[/cell][/table]

sections.title: 1. Install uv
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]1. Install uv[/b][/font_size]
uv runs the small connector program that ships in Ink Hammer's [code][color=#efe3c6]mcp[/color][/code] folder. It brings its own Python, so you do not need to install Python. Open [b][color=#efe3c6]PowerShell[/color][/b] from the Start menu and paste:

[table=1][cell bg=#26282d padding=12,8,12,8][code]powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"[/code][/cell][/table]

When it finishes, close PowerShell. uv lands in [code][color=#efe3c6]C:\Users\[i]you[/i]\.local\bin\uv.exe[/color][/code].

sections.title: 2. Turn on the Local API
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]2. Turn on the Local API[/b][/font_size]
In Ink Hammer, tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Local API for Claude[/color][/b]. It stays on between runs. It only listens on your own computer and needs a private token, which Ink Hammer writes for the connector.

sections.title: 3. Add Ink Hammer to Claude
4. Restart Claude
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]4. Restart Claude[/b][/font_size]
Quit the Claude app fully (right-click its icon by the clock, then [b][color=#efe3c6]Quit[/color][/b]) and open it again. Ink Hammer's tools now show under the connectors (tools) button in a new chat.

sections.title: Try it
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Try it[/b][/font_size]
With Ink Hammer open, ask Claude things like:

[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] "Make a 30 by 20 map of a roadside tavern at dusk with a stable and a well."[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] "Add a campfire in the yard and turn the sun down to evening."[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] "Check the walls for gaps, then export gridless at 140 px and a Universal VTT file."[/indent]

Claude drafts; you refine by hand, then export. Claude can also take screenshots of the map to check its own work.

Each Ink Hammer update brings a new connector in its [code][color=#efe3c6]mcp[/color][/code] folder: quit and reopen Claude after updating so it loads the new tools (for example round rooms and object masks).

sections.title: If it does not work
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]If it does not work[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#e8a83e]"Ink Hammer isn't answering"[/color][/b]
Ink Hammer is closed, or the Local API is off. Open Ink Hammer and tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Local API for Claude[/color][/b].

[b][color=#e8a83e]"Refused the token"[/color][/b]
Untick and tick [b][color=#efe3c6]Tools > Local API for Claude[/color][/b] again, then ask Claude to retry.

[b][color=#e8a83e]Claude does not list the Ink Hammer tools[/color][/b]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Check the paths in the config: every backslash is written twice ([code]\\[/code]).[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Check uv is where the config says: run [code]uv --version[/code] in a new PowerShell window.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Quit Claude fully and reopen it; closing the window is not enough.[/indent]

[b][color=#e8a83e]"Lost Ink Hammer during ..."[/color][/b]
Ink Hammer stopped mid-task. Restart it; your work is in the autosave if it was not saved.

[b][color=#efe3c6]Help > Connect Claude[/color][/b] in Ink Hammer shows where its token file is, if you need it.

sections.title: Overview
sections.bb:
[font_size=24][b]What's new[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]What changed in each version. Your version is in [b][color=#efe3c6]Help > About Ink Hammer[/color][/b]; [b][color=#efe3c6]Help > Check for updates[/color][/b] says whether a newer one is out. Through the guide, a New in 0.9.24 tag marks what a version added.[/color]

sections.title: 0.9.24 New in 0.9.24
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]0.9.24 New in 0.9.24[/b][/font_size]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Cliffs, dunes and hills[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Cliffs are lit by their real shape: ledges catch the light, risers turn with the sun (also by lamplight), and a shadow lies where the rock meets the ground on the shaded side. Sandstone strata and Earth bank light layer by layer. [url=cliffs.html]Cliffs, dunes and hills[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] New [b]Breakup[/b]: the ground on top breaks onto the first ledges in patches, and the ground at the foot can creep up the lowest ones. [url=cliffs.html#breakup]Breakup[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] New [b]Round top[/b] for dunes and banks: the side rolls over from the top like a dome. [url=cliffs.html#round-top]Round top[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Cliff looks retuned: Earth slope is brown earth, Grassy hill is a low hill, the rock looks have breakup on, and a new cliff starts as warm grey painted rock. Cliffs already on your maps keep their look.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Cliffs and the spills over them take [b]Opacity[/b] and [b]Tint[/b]. A cliff that had a tint saved on it now shows it.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Dune and bank sides facing the sun are lit like the sand around them (every dune had a dark ring).[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Props[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] New [b]Submerge[/b]: sink a prop into the ground from any side, with a ragged soft edge and a touch of dirt. [url=cliffs.html#submerge]Submerge[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A prop lying across the foot of a cliff no longer has a dark band cut across it.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Walls, buildings and roofs[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Flip[/b] for walls, lines, buildings and roofs, and a whole selection as one piece. [code][color=#efe3c6]F[/color][/code] flips a building or roof. [url=walls.html#flip]Flip[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b]Lift[/b] for walls: railings, beams and screens hang off the ground. [url=walls.html#lift]Lift[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Drawn roofs take [b]Blend[/b] (Multiply, Add, Subtract); roof layers take every blend. [url=walls.html#roof-blend]Roof blend[/url][/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Walls and buildings with [b][color=#efe3c6]Casts shadow[/color][/b] off no longer throw shadows in the 3D lighting.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Water[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The sea: waves keep their direction past ships and rocks, crests and troughs show in a still, a ship's wake fades into dashes. The sea looks are retuned to one painted style.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Rivers show which way they flow. Clear stream, Lake, Murky river and Swamp have the painted look; banks have light shallows and brush-stroke ripples.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Waterfalls break into falling strands, show a bright roll over the lip and take the colour of the water they pour into. Spills over cliffs land in smooth broken white water, and rocks show through the water running over them.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Selecting and Properties[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A box drag picks everything it touches by its real shape.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] With different kinds of things selected, Properties shows only the settings they all have. Every kind of thing shows its settings in the same order, and settings that do nothing for it are hidden.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] A turned building's selection box turns with it. [code][color=#efe3c6]R[/color][/code] and [code][color=#efe3c6][lb][/color][/code] [code][color=#efe3c6][rb][/color][/code] turn and scale a building like the mouse does.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Waterfalls, fire and cliffs are clicked near their centre line, so small falls stay easy to pick.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Properties gets most of the right column; the 3D view starts folded.[/indent]

[font_size=16][b][color=#e8a83e]Speed and fixes[/color][/b][/font_size]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Maps open about a third faster.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Water no longer flashes white as a map opens, and the map no longer blinks a few seconds after opening.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Several undo fixes: a coast, a sea look change and the Fog command are each one [code][color=#efe3c6]Ctrl[/color][/code]+[code][color=#efe3c6]Z[/color][/code].[/indent]

[font_size=24][b]Troubleshooting[/b][/font_size]
[color=#a3a09a]The usual problems and their fixes. Click a question to open it.[/color]

sections.title: Lighting
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Lighting[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#e8a83e]I don't see any sun shadows[/color][/b]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The sun switch at the top right (the first of the speed switches) may be off. The Lights panel says so and has a [b][color=#efe3c6]Show sun shadows[/color][/b] button. See [url=lighting.html#speed-switches]Speed switches[/url].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] In the Lights tool, check [b][color=#efe3c6]On[/color][/b] and [b][color=#efe3c6]Cast shadows[/color][/b] under Master light.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] With [b][color=#efe3c6]Daylight[/color][/b] at 100% shadows are faint. Lower it, or raise [b][color=#efe3c6]Shadow depth[/color][/b].[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The object needs a height: props use [b][color=#efe3c6]Height (ft)[/color][/b], and the layer needs [b][color=#efe3c6]Casts sun shadows[/color][/b].[/indent]

[b][color=#e8a83e]A lamp does not light something[/color][/b]
With 3D lighting (the default) a lamp lights by height: check the lamp's [b][color=#efe3c6]Height[/color][/b] and whether a wall, roof or tall prop is between them. With classic 2D lighting a lamp lights only its own layer and the layers under it: drag the lamp's layer above the thing it should light, or move the thing to a lower layer. See [url=lighting.html#layer-order]Light and layer order[/url].

[b][color=#e8a83e]Everything is dark inside a building[/color][/b]
Buildings keep the sun out (as if roofed), so the inside only gets daylight and lamps. Add lamps inside, or select the building and untick [b][color=#efe3c6]Roofed[/color][/b] for an open ruin.

sections.title: Speed
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Speed[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#e8a83e]The editor feels slow[/color][/b]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] [b][color=#efe3c6]View > Fast editing[/color][/b] turns heavy effects off and draws at 50%. [b][color=#efe3c6]View > Full quality[/color][/b] puts them back.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Or turn single speed switches off at the top right: animation and contact shade cost the most on big maps.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] Lower the render scale (the % box at the top right). The map looks softer; exports are not affected.[/indent]
[indent][color=#e8a83e]•[/color] The status bar shows frames per second and how long the map takes to draw, so you can see what helped.[/indent]

[b][color=#e8a83e]The map looks soft or blurry[/color][/b]
The render scale (top right) is below 100%, or Fast editing is on. Set it back to 100% or use [b][color=#efe3c6]View > Full quality[/color][/b].

sections.title: Files
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Files[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#e8a83e]Ink Hammer closed and I lost my work[/color][/b]
Start Ink Hammer again. If there is an autosaved copy newer than your file, it asks [b][color=#efe3c6]Recover unsaved work[/color][/b]. Click [b][color=#efe3c6]Recover[/color][/b], then save. Ink Hammer autosaves every 2 minutes.

Your last saved version is also kept beside the map as a [code].bak[/code] file.

[b][color=#e8a83e]Art is missing when I open a map on another computer[/color][/b]
Package the map on the first computer with [b][color=#efe3c6]File > Package map with its assets[/color][/b], then open the packaged copy.

[b][color=#e8a83e]Windows won't start Ink Hammer.exe[/color][/b]
On the [b][color=#efe3c6]Windows protected your PC[/color][/b] screen click [b][color=#efe3c6]More info[/color][/b], then [b][color=#efe3c6]Run anyway[/color][/b]. The beta is not code-signed yet.

sections.title: Reporting a bug
sections.bb:
[font_size=19][b]Reporting a bug[/b][/font_size]
[b][color=#efe3c6]Help > Report a bug...[/color][/b] opens a short form: the area, what happened, the steps, how to reach you and an optional picture. Your Ink Hammer version, Windows version and graphics card are added for you. [b][color=#efe3c6]Send[/color][/b] sends it; [b][color=#efe3c6]Copy instead[/color][/b] copies it all: paste it into #bug-reports on the Anvil N Ink Discord if sending does not work.
